curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Start with what driver assistance systems do and do not do, then passive warning systems, back-up and blind spot warnings, rear, side and surround cameras, and curve speed warnings.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: One card per system; contrast cards for a back-up warning versus a rear camera and for passive warnings versus systems that act.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz naming a system and asking what it does and what the driver must still do.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Cover pedestrian, bicycle and obstacle detection and its beeps, forward collision and lane departure warnings, parking sensors, rear cross-traffic alerts and high speed alerts.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: Cards for each warning; contrast cards for continuous detection beeps versus a constant parking-sensor tone.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz describing an alert and asking what it means.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Explain assistance technologies and safety-critical systems: automatic emergency braking, automatic reverse braking, lane keeping assist, left turn crash avoidance, and how the road test treats them.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: Cards for each assist system; contrast cards for warning-only systems versus systems that brake or steer.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on which systems act on their own and what the driver must still do.

curriculum_unit_hints.session_strategy: Cover convenience technologies and the testing restriction, adaptive cruise control, automatic parallel parking, and Nevada's definition of an autonomous vehicle with the automation levels.
curriculum_unit_hints.flashcard_strategy: Cards for each convenience feature and the autonomy rules; a contrast card for the autonomous-vehicle levels versus the full level scale.
curriculum_unit_hints.quiz_strategy: Hub-chosen quiz on convenience features and autonomous-vehicle levels.
